competitive_position.claim: The company is a small, externally managed REIT whose assets are all in New York City. Vornado manages, leases and develops its properties, so its position rests on the quality of its Manhattan and Queens real estate and on Vornado's services, not on its own operating platform.
quotes: We are managed by, and our properties are leased and developed by, Vornado Realty Trust (“Vornado”) (NYSE: VNO).
All of our properties are in New York City and are affected by the economic cycles and risks inherent to this area.

competitive_position.claim: The main support for the competitive position is Bloomberg, which occupies all of the office space at 731 Lexington Avenue. Bloomberg was 55% of rental revenues in the nine months to September 30, 2026, against 60% a year earlier. Its revenue was $99,004,000, against $96,655,000. This is also the largest dependency.
quotes: If we were to lose Bloomberg as a tenant, or if Bloomberg were to be unable to fulfill its obligations under its lease, it would adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

competitive_position.claim: Bloomberg's lease was extended to February 2040, which gives long-dated tenure for the main office asset. A March 2026 amendment then gave Bloomberg a rent abatement of $56,809,000, which cut its tenant fund from $113,618,000 to $56,809,000.
quotes: In May 2024, Alexander’s and Bloomberg entered into an agreement to extend Bloomberg’s leases that were scheduled to expire in February 2029 for a term of eleven years to February 2040.

competitive_position.claim: Occupancy is high. The commercial occupancy rate was 94.6% and the residential occupancy rate was 98.1% at September 30, 2026, against 94.6% and 97.7% at December 31, 2025.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, the commercial occupancy rate was 94.6% and the residential occupancy rate was 98.1%.

competitive_position.claim: The company re-tenanted a Rego Park anchor box. Kohl's terminated its lease on August 2, 2026 and paid the remaining $25,100,000 of a $29,000,000 termination payment, and the company signed a new long-term lease with Target for the same space.
quotes: Simultaneously, we entered into a 15-year lease, plus renewal options, with Target for that space.

competitive_position.basis: inferred from the income statement, the cash flow statement and the MD&A explanation

Nine-month net cash from operating activities was $29,913 (table in thousands), against $50,020.
quotes: $18,800,000 of higher straight-line revenue resulting from Kohl’s lease modification at the Rego Park shopping center

competitive_position.claim: The company sold its vacant Rego Park I property, which turned an underused asset into cash. Cash and cash equivalents were $299,789 (table in thousands) at September 30, 2026, against $128,167 at December 31, 2025.
quotes: On May 28, 2026, we completed the sale of our Rego Park I property, located in Queens, New York, for $235,500,000, with total proceeds of $202,750,000, net of costs, and a financial statement gain of $148,002,000.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items; the effect on concentration is inferred

quotes: Our portfolio is comprised of four properties aggregating 2,106,000 square feet.

competitive_position.claim: Retail space at 731 Lexington Avenue is a weak spot. The Home Depot lease expired on January 31, 2025, and the nine-month rental revenue comparison cites lower revenue from that expiration and other retail tenant expirations there.
quotes: On January 31, 2025, Home Depot’s 83,000 square foot lease at the retail portion of our 731 Lexington Avenue property expired.
Annual rental revenues from Home Depot were approximately $15,000,000.

competitive_position.claim: The company names competition and office-market trends as threats. We compete with a large number of real estate investors, property owners and developers, some of whom may be willing to accept lower returns on their investments.
We may be adversely affected by trends in office real estate.
